Goal: I can copy an angle and use it to construct a parallel line, with informal reasoning (copying justified in 4.13, parallel test proved in 5.6).

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
To copy an angle at a new vertex: draw an arc across the given angle, then the same arc from the new vertex. Measure the opening between the arc's crossing points with the compass and transfer it. The ray through the new crossing point makes an equal angle (justified in 4.13).

To draw a line through P parallel to l: draw any line through P that crosses l. Copy the angle it makes with l so that the copy sits at P in the corresponding position. The new line is parallel to l because corresponding angles are equal, a test we prove in 5.6.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
